l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: Jesus Christ declares the signs, judgments, covenants, gathering, and future work of the Father. He promises to be in the midst of the gathered people and to go before them and be their rearward.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The Father will gather the dispersed house of Israel, establish Zion, fulfill his covenant, and prepare the way for his people to come to Jesus Christ. He will show his power, establish the church among those who repent, and execute vengeance upon those who refuse to repent.

l: house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The house of Israel will be gathered from its dispersion, and a remnant will receive the land of its inheritance. Those who repent and hearken will be numbered among the people of the covenant.

l: the remnant of the house of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The remnant of Jacob will be among the Gentiles and will have power over its adversaries. It will assist in building the New Jerusalem and gathering the dispersed people.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The Gentiles will receive the works and words brought forth from them, and these things will be a sign concerning the house of Israel. If they do not harden their hearts, they may repent, be baptized in Jesus Christ’s name, know the true points of his doctrine, and be numbered among the house of Israel; otherwise they will face destruction and be cut off.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: My people will be gathered from their long dispersion and established in Zion. Those who refuse to repent will be cut off from among them, while those who repent may be numbered among them.

l: the servant, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The servant will declare the work among the Gentiles and will bring forth Jesus Christ’s words with power. His life will be in Jesus Christ’s hand; he will be marred because of them, but Jesus Christ will heal him.

l: Zion, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: Zion will be established again among the house of Israel when the dispersed people are gathered.

l: New Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The New Jerusalem will be built by the remnant of Jacob, the house of Israel, and those who assist them. The dispersed people will be gathered into it.

l: the promised land, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: This land is given to the remnant of Jacob for its inheritance. The people will build a city called the New Jerusalem upon it.

l: the covenant with the people Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The covenant of the Father will be fulfilled through works that come forth from the Gentiles to the seed of the house of Israel. Those who repent and hearken will come into the covenant.

l: the work of the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The work of the Father will commence among the remnant of Jacob, the dispersed tribes, and all nations. It will prepare the way for the people to come to Jesus Christ and be gathered to their land of inheritance.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The gospel will be preached among the remnant of Jacob, beginning the work of the Father among that people and the dispersed house of Israel.

l: the church of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The Father will establish the church among the Gentiles if they repent, hearken to his words, and do not harden their hearts.

l: gathering of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The gathering will bring the dispersed house of Israel and the tribes that were lost back to the land of their inheritance. The remnant of Jacob and others who repent will assist in this gathering into the New Jerusalem.

l: building the New Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The remnant of Jacob and the house of Israel will build a city called the New Jerusalem. Those who repent and are numbered among the remnant will assist in the building.

l: sin and corruption, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: Lyings, deceivings, envyings, strifes, priestcrafts, and whoredoms will be done away. Witchcrafts, soothsayers, graven images, standing images, and the works of people’s hands will be cut off.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The Gentiles are called to repent, come unto Jesus Christ, be baptized in his name, and know the true points of his doctrine. Those who repent and hearken will be numbered among the house of Israel, while those who do not repent will be cut off.

l: New Jerusalem gathering, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 21
s: The people scattered across the land will be gathered into the New Jerusalem. The power of heaven will come down among them, and Jesus Christ will be in their midst.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The Lord speaks to a barren and forsaken woman, calling her his wife and promising to gather her with great mercies and everlasting kindness. He promises that her children will increase, inherit the Gentiles, and be taught of the Lord with great peace. The Lord will establish the woman in righteousness, protect her from oppression and terror, and cause those who gather against her to fall. He declares that no weapon formed against the Lord’s servants will prosper and that their righteousness is of him.

l: the Son of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The Lord calls the barren woman his wife and promises to gather her, show her everlasting kindness, and have mercy on her. He promises to establish her in righteousness, protect her from oppression and terror, and cause those who gather against her to fall.

l: woman (the Lord's wife), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The woman is described as barren, forsaken, grieved in spirit, and refused, but the Lord calls her his wife. She is promised restoration, expansion, protection, and freedom from shame and reproach.

l: children (the woman's children), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The woman's children will be more numerous than the children of the married wife. They will inherit the Gentiles, be taught of the Lord, and have great peace.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The Gentiles will be inherited by the woman's seed.

l: the Lord's kindness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The Lord's kindness will not depart from the woman, even though the mountains depart and the hills are removed.

l: the Lord's mercy, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The Lord promises to gather the woman with great mercies and to have everlasting mercy on her.

l: the Lord's covenant of peace, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The Lord's covenant of peace will not be removed from the woman.

l: weapon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: No weapon formed against the Lord's servants will prosper.

l: servants of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The servants of the Lord receive the heritage that no weapon formed against them will prosper and that every tongue reviling them in judgment will be condemned.

l: righteousness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 22
s: The woman will be established in righteousness, and the righteousness of the Lord's servants is of the Lord.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Jesus commands the people to search the words of Isaiah diligently because they concern the house of Israel and the Gentiles. He teaches that those who hearken to his words, repent, and are baptized shall be saved. Jesus explains that Samuel the Lamanite prophesied that many saints would arise from the dead and minister to many, and he commands that this event be written in the record. He also commands the people to teach the things he has expounded from the scriptures.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Jesus commands the people to search the things he has taught, write them, and teach the things he has expounded from the scriptures. He reminds them that Samuel the Lamanite prophesied that many saints would arise from the dead and minister to many, and he commands that this be written.

l: Isaiah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Isaiah spoke concerning all things relating to the people of the house of Israel, and therefore also spoke concerning the Gentiles. His words are described as great and are to be searched diligently.

l: house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: The house of Israel is identified as the people concerning whom Isaiah spoke.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: The Gentiles are among those concerning whom Isaiah spoke. The things Jesus taught are to go forth to the Gentiles according to the time and will of the Father.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: The Father will determine, according to his time and will, when the written things go forth to the Gentiles. The Father will glorify his name in Jesus at the time when many saints arise from the dead.

l: Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Nephi brings forth the record he has kept when Jesus commands him to do so. Nephi remembers that the rising and ministering of many saints had not been written.

l: Samuel the Lamanite, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Samuel the Lamanite was commanded to testify to the people that many saints would arise from the dead, appear to many, and minister to them. His prophecy was fulfilled according to Jesus's words.

l: saints, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Many saints arose from the dead, appeared to many, and ministered to them. This event had not initially been written in the record, so Jesus commanded that it be recorded.

l: the plates of brass, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Jesus expounds all the scriptures that the people had received and commands them to teach the things he has expounded. The scriptures include the things that had been written and the other scriptures Jesus wanted written.

l: the record, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Jesus commands Nephi to bring forth the record he has kept. After learning that the rising and ministering of many saints was not recorded, Jesus commands that it be written in the record.

l: words, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 23
s: Jesus commands the people to give heed to his words and says that those who hearken to his words, repent, and are baptized shall be saved. The words spoken by Isaiah have been and shall be fulfilled.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The Father gives words to Malachi concerning a messenger who will prepare the way and the messenger of the covenant who will come to the temple. The Lord of Hosts will refine, judge, and witness against those who commit wrongdoing, while purifying the sons of Levi. The Lord calls the people to return by bringing tithes and offerings, promising protection and a blessing. Those who fear the Lord will be remembered as his jewels and spared, and the righteous will be distinguished from the wicked.

l: Malachi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: Malachi is the one to whom the Father gives words that are written and later expounded.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The Father gives Malachi words declaring that he will send a messenger to prepare the way.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The Lord of Hosts says that he will come to judgment, witness against wrongdoing, rebuke the devourer, and open the windows of heaven with a blessing. He says that he does not change and calls the people to return to him.

l: the messenger, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The messenger is sent by the Father to prepare the way before him.

l: the messenger of the covenant, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The messenger of the covenant, whom the people delight in, will suddenly come to the temple.

l: the day of his coming, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The day of his coming is difficult to abide, and those present will face refining and purification like refiner’s fire and fuller’s soap.

l: judgment, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The Lord will come near to judgment and be a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, oppressors, those who turn aside the stranger, and those who do not fear him.

l: return to the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The people are told to return to the Lord, with the promise that he will return to them.

l: tithes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The people rob God in tithes and are told to bring all the tithes into the storehouse.

l: offerings, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The people rob God in offerings, and the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will become pleasant to the Lord as in former years.

l: a blessing, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The Lord promises to open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing so abundant that there will not be room enough to receive it.

l: the ordinances, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The people have gone away from the ordinances of their fathers and have not kept them.

l: righteousness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: The sons of Levi will be purified so that they may offer an offering to the Lord in righteousness.

l: service to God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 24
s: Some say that it is vain to serve God and question the profit of keeping his ordinances and walking mournfully before the Lord of Hosts.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: The day of the Lord will burn the proud and those who do wickedly, leaving them neither root nor branch. Those who fear the Lord’s name will receive healing from the Son of Righteousness and will tread down the wicked. The law of Moses, given in Horeb for all Israel, is to be remembered. Elijah the prophet will be sent before the great and dreadful day of the Lord to turn the hearts of fathers and children toward one another.

l: the day of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: The day of the Lord is described as great and dreadful. Before it comes, Elijah the prophet will be sent, and on that day the wicked will be burned and the righteous will tread them down.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: The Lord of Hosts declares that the day will burn up the proud and those who do wickedly, leaving them neither root nor branch. He says that those who fear his name will receive healing and that the wicked will be ashes under their feet.

l: Son of Righteousness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: The Son of Righteousness will arise for those who fear the Lord’s name, bringing healing in his wings.

l: the law of Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: The law of Moses is to be remembered. It was commanded to Moses in Horeb for all Israel, with statutes and judgments.

l: Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: Moses is identified as the Lord’s servant. The law was commanded to him in Horeb for all Israel.

l: Elijah the prophet, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 25
s: Elijah the prophet will be sent before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord. He will turn the heart of the fathers to the children and the heart of the children to their fathers.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Jesus expounded the scriptures and taught the multitude about events from the beginning until the last day, including judgment and the resurrections. Mormon wrote that only a small part of Jesus’s teachings could be included, and that greater things would be made manifest if the people believed what had first been given to them. Jesus taught and ministered to the multitude and their children, healed many, raised a man from the dead, and ascended into heaven. The disciples baptized and taught the people, who were filled with the Holy Ghost, taught and ministered to one another, dealt justly, and did as Jesus commanded.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Jesus expounded the scriptures and taught the multitude all things, from the beginning until the time of his coming in glory and the last day. He taught and ministered to the children, healed the sick and afflicted, raised a man from the dead, broke and blessed bread, and ascended into heaven.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The Father commanded that the scriptures be given to Jesus for future generations.

l: the Son of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The Lord forbade Mormon to write all the things engraven upon the plates of Nephi, saying that he would try the faith of his people. Mormon wrote the things commanded him of the Lord.

l: God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: All people, kindreds, nations, and tongues shall stand before God to be judged of their works.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Christ was before the world began, and mercy, justice, and holiness are in Christ.

l: Mormon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Mormon wrote a lesser part of the things Jesus taught and made an end of his sayings before proceeding to write the things commanded him.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The multitude heard Jesus expound the scriptures and later gathered to see and hear the children utter marvelous things.

l: the people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The people were taught by Jesus, and some of them were baptized and filled with the Holy Ghost. They taught and ministered one to another, had all things common, dealt justly, and did all things Jesus commanded.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The things Mormon wrote were to be brought again unto the people from the Gentiles, according to the words Jesus had spoken.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The disciples whom Jesus had chosen began to baptize and teach as many as came unto them.

l: the children, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Jesus taught and ministered to the children of the multitude and loosed their tongues. The children, including babes, uttered great and marvelous things that were forbidden to be written.

l: the church of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Those baptized in the name of Jesus were called the church of Christ.

l: the scriptures, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The Father commanded that the scriptures be given to Jesus for future generations. Jesus expounded the scriptures to the multitude.

l: the plates of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The plates of Nephi contain the greater part of the things Jesus taught the people.

l: earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The earth shall be wrapped together as a scroll and pass away when the elements melt with fervent heat.

l: resurrection of everlasting life, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Those whose works are good shall come forth to the resurrection of everlasting life.

l: resurrection of damnation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Those whose works are evil shall come forth to the resurrection of damnation.

l: faith, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The Lord said that he would try the faith of his people. If the people believe the things first given to them, greater things shall be made manifest; if they do not believe, the greater things shall be withheld unto their condemnation.

l: the greater things, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The greater things shall be made manifest to the people if they believe the things first given to them. If they do not believe, the greater things shall be withheld from them unto their condemnation.

l: the things Jesus taught, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Only a hundredth part of the things Jesus taught could be written in the book. The plates of Nephi contain the more part of his teachings, while Mormon wrote a lesser part.

l: three days of teaching, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Jesus truly taught the people for the space of three days.

l: the ascension of Christ into heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: Jesus ascended into heaven after showing himself to the multitude, healing their sick and afflicted, raising a man from the dead, and showing forth his power.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: The disciples baptized those who came unto them, and those baptized in the name of Jesus were filled with the Holy Ghost and called the church of Christ.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 26
s: As many as were baptized in the name of Jesus were filled with the Holy Ghost.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The disciples of Jesus pray, fast, preach, baptize, and ask Jesus what to call the church. Jesus teaches that the church must be called in his name and built upon his gospel, and he explains that repentance, baptism, endurance, and faithfulness are required for salvation. He commands the disciples to write what they see and hear, says that people will be judged by their works, and promises that requests made to the Father in his name will be answered. Jesus contrasts the strait gate and narrow way leading to life with the broad way leading to death, and warns about the fourth generation being led away.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Jesus appears among the disciples, teaches them what to call the church, gives them his gospel and commandments, and promises that requests made to the Father in his name will be given. He says that he will judge the world and that people must be like him.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The disciples of Jesus journey, preach what they have heard and seen, baptize in the name of Jesus, and unite in prayer and fasting. Jesus commands them to write what they see and hear and to judge the people according to his judgment.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The Father sent Jesus to do his will and to be lifted up upon the cross. The Father will bless the church for Jesus’s sake, hear prayers made in Jesus’s name, show forth his works in the church, and judge the world.

l: the church of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The church is to be called in the name of Jesus and must be built upon his gospel. If it is built upon the works of men or the devil, its works will end and it will be cast into the fire.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The people dispute about the name of the church, and the works of the people are to be written. Their works will be known through the books and will be part of their judgment.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The gospel given by Jesus is that he came into the world to do the will of the Father, was lifted up upon the cross, and draws all men to be judged according to their works. Those in the church are told to do the works they have seen Jesus do.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Baptism in the name of Jesus is required for those who repent. Through baptism and the reception of the Holy Ghost, people may be sanctified and stand spotless before Jesus.

l: name of Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The name of Jesus is the name by which the church must be called and by which people must take upon themselves his name. The Father will hear and answer prayers made in this name.

l: children of men, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Men lift Jesus up upon the cross, and the Father will lift men up to stand before Jesus for judgment. Men are also commanded to do the works they have seen Jesus do.

l: cross, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Jesus is sent by the Father to be lifted up upon the cross. After being lifted up, he draws all men unto him so they can be judged according to their works.

l: judgment, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Judgment is according to works, and Jesus will judge the world before the Father. The disciples will judge the people according to the judgment Jesus gives them.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Those who repent and are baptized in the name of Jesus may be filled and held guiltless if they endure to the end. Repentance from all sins is part of washing garments in Jesus’s blood.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The reception of the Holy Ghost sanctifies those who repent and are baptized in the name of Jesus so that they may stand spotless before him at the last day.

l: kingdom of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: No unclean thing can enter the kingdom of the Father. Only those who have washed their garments in Jesus’s blood through faith, repentance, and faithfulness to the end enter his rest.

l: blood of Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: People enter the rest of the Father by washing their garments in the blood of Jesus because of their faith, repentance of all their sins, and faithfulness to the end.

l: the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Jesus came into the world to do the will of the Father and will draw all men to be judged. The world will be judged from the books that are written.

l: books, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The books that have been written and will be written contain records by which the works of the people and the world will be known and judged. All things are written by the Father.

l: generation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Jesus says that he, the Father, and the holy angels rejoice because none of the people of this generation are lost. He says that this generation gives him fulness of joy.

l: fourth generation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The fourth generation from the current generation causes Jesus sorrow because its people are led away captive. They will sell him for silver, gold, and corruptible or stolen things, and their works will be turned upon their own heads.

l: strait gate, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Jesus commands people to enter through the strait gate. The strait gate is associated with the narrow way that leads to life.

l: narrow way, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The narrow way leads to life, and few people find it.

l: broad way, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: The broad way leads to death, and many people travel in it until the night comes, when no man can work.

l: life, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Life is reached through the strait gate and narrow way, which few people find.

l: death, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 27
s: Death is reached through the broad way, which many people travel.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: Jesus asks his disciples what they desire after he returns to the Father. Most desire to end their ministry after reaching the age of man and come to Jesus in his kingdom, while three disciples desire to remain until they bring the souls of men to him. Jesus promises the three disciples that they will not taste death, and they are changed so they can minister among the people without pain or sorrow except for the sins of the world. Mormon records that the three disciples minister among the Gentiles, Jews, scattered tribes of Israel, and all nations, while the people of Nephi are converted and united to the church of Christ.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: Jesus asks the disciples what they desire after he is gone to the Father. He promises the three disciples that they will not taste death, will minister to bring souls to him, and will receive a greater change at the judgment day of Christ.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The disciples tell Jesus that they desire their ministry to end after they have lived to the age of man so they can come to him in his kingdom. Jesus tells them that after they are seventy and two years old they will come to him and find rest.

l: the three disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples desire to remain and bring the souls of men to Jesus while the world stands. They are changed, minister among the people, suffer no pain or sorrow except for the sins of the world, and are to remain in that state until the judgment day of Christ.

l: the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The Father gives the Holy Ghost to the children of men because of Jesus. The three disciples behold the doings of the Father unto the children of men until all things are fulfilled according to his will.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The Holy Ghost bears record of the Father and Jesus. Those who are baptized through the ministry of the three disciples receive the Holy Ghost.

l: Mormon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: Mormon ends his account of these things for a time and does not write the names of the three who were never to taste of death because the Lord forbade it. He has seen the three disciples and says they minister among the Gentiles, Jews, and all nations.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples will be among the Gentiles, though the Gentiles will not know them. A great and marvelous work will be wrought among the Gentiles by them before the judgment day.

l: the people of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples go among all the people of Nephi and preach the gospel of Christ. The people are converted to the Lord, united to the church of Christ, and blessed according to Jesus's word.

l: the church of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: Those who believe the preaching of the three disciples are baptized, receive the Holy Ghost, and are united to the church of Christ. People who do not belong to the church cast the three disciples into prisons and other places, but cannot hold them.

l: heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples are caught up into heaven and see and hear unspeakable things. They are forbidden and not given power to speak of what they saw and heard.

l: the kingdom of the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The disciples who desire to end their ministry are promised rest with Jesus in his kingdom. The three disciples will have fulness of joy, sit in the kingdom of the Father, and at the judgment day be received into it eternally.

l: Jesus's ministry, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The disciples ask that their ministry end after they have lived to the age of man. The three disciples continue their ministry by preaching, baptizing, and uniting believers to the church.

l: death, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples are promised that they will never taste of death and will not endure its pains. Mormon learns that a change was necessary so they would not taste death.

l: immortality, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples are changed from mortality toward an immortal state and are sanctified in the flesh. Their change is not equal to the greater change that will take place at the last day.

l: the change wrought upon the three disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The change wrought upon the three disciples prevents them from suffering pain or sorrow except for the sins of the world and keeps Satan from having power to tempt them. It also makes them holy and prevents the powers of the earth from holding them, until they receive a greater change at the judgment day of Christ.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: The three disciples preach the gospel of Christ to all the people of Nephi and to all people upon the face of the land. Those who accept it are converted to the Lord and united to the church of Christ.

l: the judgment day of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 28
s: Before the judgment day of Christ, the three disciples will perform great and marvelous works and bring many souls to Jesus. At that day they will receive a greater change and be received into the kingdom of the Father to dwell eternally in the heavens.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The unit concerns the Lord’s covenant with the children of Israel and its fulfillment when these sayings come to the Gentiles. It teaches that the words of the Lord spoken by the holy prophets will be fulfilled and that the Lord remembers his covenant with the house of Israel. It warns against spurning the doings of the Lord, denying Jesus Christ, rejecting revelation and spiritual gifts, or denying miracles. It also says that the Lord will execute judgment and fulfill his covenant with the house of Israel.

l: the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The Lord will fulfill the words spoken by the holy prophets, remember his covenant with the house of Israel, and execute judgment. He will cause his justice to overtake those who spurn his doings.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The Gentiles will receive these sayings according to the word of the Lord.

l: Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The children of Israel are the people concerning whom the Father made a covenant about restoration to the lands of their inheritance. The fulfillment of that covenant is already beginning when these sayings come to the Gentiles.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The house of Israel is the people with whom the Lord has made a covenant that he will remember and fulfill. The Lord will do unto them according to that which he has sworn.

l: the covenant with the people Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The covenant concerns the restoration of the children of Israel to the lands of their inheritance. The Lord remembers it and will fulfill it.

l: restoration of the house of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: Restoration concerns the children of Israel returning to the lands of their inheritance. Its fulfillment is already beginning when these sayings come to the Gentiles.

l: these sayings, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: These sayings will come to the Gentiles according to the word of the Lord. Their coming forth indicates that the covenant concerning the restoration of the children of Israel is beginning to be fulfilled.

l: the words of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The words of the Lord spoken by the holy prophets will all be fulfilled. They should not be considered vain or delayed.

l: the doings of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The doings of the Lord should not be spurned, denied, hissed at, or made game of. Those who spurn them will be overtaken by the sword of his justice.

l: Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: Jesus Christ and his works should not be denied. The text warns against saying that no miracle can be wrought by Jesus Christ.

l: miracles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: Miracles can be wrought by Jesus Christ. The text warns that one who says for gain that no miracle can be wrought by him shall become like unto the son of perdition.

l: judgment, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 29
s: The Lord’s judgment will be executed to the fulfilling of the covenant made unto the house of Israel. His sword of justice will soon overtake those who spurn his doings.

l: The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, commands that the Gentiles be addressed. The Gentiles are told to turn from their wicked ways and repent of their evil doings and abominations. They are instructed to come unto Jesus Christ and be baptized in his name. Through baptism, they may receive a remission of their sins, be filled with the Holy Ghost, and be numbered with the people who are of the house of Israel.

l: Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, commands that the Gentiles be told to turn from their wicked ways, repent, come unto him, and be baptized in his name.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: The Gentiles are commanded to turn from their wicked ways and repent of their evil doings, including lyings, deceivings, whoredoms, secret abominations, idolatries, murders, priestcrafts, envyings, strifes, and other wickedness. They are told to come unto Jesus Christ and be baptized in his name so that they may receive a remission of their sins, be filled with the Holy Ghost, and be numbered with the people who are of the house of Israel.

l: house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: The house of Israel is the house whose people may include the Gentiles after they receive a remission of their sins and are filled with the Holy Ghost.

l: repentance, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: Repentance concerns turning from wicked ways and from evil doings, wickedness, and abominations.

l: baptism, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: Baptism in the name of Jesus Christ is commanded for the Gentiles after they turn from their wicked ways and repent. Through it, they may receive a remission of their sins and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

l: remission of sins, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: A remission of sins may be received by the Gentiles when they come unto Jesus Christ and are baptized in his name.

l: sin, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: The Gentiles are told to receive a remission of their sins through baptism in the name of Jesus Christ.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: The Holy Ghost may fill the Gentiles after they receive a remission of their sins through baptism in the name of Jesus Christ.

l: the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman, Chapter 30
s: The Gentiles may be numbered with the people who are of the house of Israel after they receive a remission of their sins and are filled with the Holy Ghost.

l: The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The people were converted unto the Lord and lived in peace, sharing their goods and receiving blessings, while the disciples of Jesus performed miracles. The people of Nephi prospered, rebuilt cities, and became rich, but later pride, divisions, churches, wickedness, and secret combinations spread among them and the Lamanites. The Nephites and Lamanites became exceedingly wicked, while the disciples of Jesus remained righteous and continued to suffer persecution. Nephi, Amos, and Ammaron kept the records, and Ammaron hid the sacred records after three hundred and twenty years from the coming of Christ.

l: Jesus, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Jesus was the one in whose name the disciples worked miracles. The people who believed in Jesus were called true believers and true worshipers of Christ.

l: the disciples of Jesus, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The disciples of Jesus formed a church of Christ, baptized those who repented, and saw them receive the Holy Ghost. They healed the sick, raised the dead, and performed many other miracles in the name of Jesus. The disciples who remained were persecuted, imprisoned, cast into furnaces and dens of wild beasts, and continued doing miracles without being harmed.

l: the church of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The disciples of Jesus formed a church of Christ in all the surrounding lands. The true church was later denied and persecuted by other churches, while its disciples remained humble and believed in Christ.

l: the people of Nephi, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The people of Nephi were converted unto the Lord, became strong, multiplied, and became fair and delightsome. They rebuilt cities, including Zarahemla, and were blessed in marriage and according to the Lord’s promises. Later, they became proud because of their riches and became exceedingly wicked like the Lamanites.

l: the Lamanites, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The Lamanites were converted unto the Lord with the Nephites, and there was peace between them. Later, some people took upon themselves the name of Lamanites, and the Lamanites became proud, wicked, and taught their children to reject the gospel of Christ.

l: Nephites, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The true believers in Christ were called Nephites, along with Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites. The Nephites later became exceedingly wicked like the Lamanites.

l: the children of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The people who were in one and free from robbers, murderers, and divisions were called the children of Christ and heirs to the kingdom of God.

l: the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The people were converted, had all things common, dealt justly, and lived without contention for many years. Later, they became divided into classes, built churches for gain, and became increasingly wicked.

l: the wicked part of the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The wicked part of the people became more numerous and stronger than the people of God. They built churches, adorned them with precious things, and later built up the secret oaths and combinations of Gadianton.

l: the robbers of Gadianton, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The robbers of Gadianton spread over all the land after three hundred years had passed away. They trafficked in all manner of traffic and laid up gold and silver in abundance.

l: Nephi, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Nephi kept the last record upon the plates of Nephi. He died after the first generation from Christ had passed away, and his son Amos kept the record in his stead.

l: Amos, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Amos kept the record upon the plates of Nephi for eighty-four years after Nephi died. Amos later died, and his son Amos kept the record; that Amos eventually died after three hundred and five years had passed away.

l: Ammaron, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Ammaron kept the record after his brother Amos died. Constrained by the Holy Ghost, he hid up the sacred records after three hundred and twenty years had passed away.

l: the land, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The land had no contention during the people’s period of peace, and cities were rebuilt where cities had been burned. Some cities had been sunk and could not be renewed. Later, the land was filled with many churches, wickedness, and robbers of Gadianton.

l: the plates of Nephi, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Nephi kept the last record upon the plates of Nephi. Amos and his son Amos also kept the record upon the plates of Nephi.

l: the records, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The records were handed down from generation to generation and included sacred records. Ammaron hid them up unto the Lord so they could come again unto the remnant of the house of Jacob.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Those who repented and were baptized received the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost constrained Ammaron to hide up the sacred records.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The people who rejected the gospel of Christ were called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites. They wilfully rebelled against it and taught their children not to believe.

l: the conversion of the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: In the thirty and sixth year, all the people across the land, both Nephites and Lamanites, were converted unto the Lord. They had no contentions or disputations and dealt justly with one another.

l: peace, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Peace continued in the land for many years, and there was no contention among the people because of the love of God in their hearts. Peace later remained for a small part of the people even after some revolted from the church.

l: miracles, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The disciples of Jesus performed great and marvelous works, including healing the sick, raising the dead, and causing the lame, blind, and deaf to receive healing. They worked miracles only in the name of Jesus, and their miracles continued despite persecution.

l: the coming of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The records mark the passing of years from the coming of Christ. Ammaron hid the sacred records in the three hundred and twentieth year from the coming of Christ.

l: the love of God, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The love of God dwelled in the hearts of the people and caused there to be no contention in the land.

l: the churches that professed to know Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: Many churches professed to know Christ while denying most parts of his gospel. They received all manner of wickedness and administered sacred things to those forbidden to receive them because of unworthiness.

l: the riches of the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The people became exceedingly rich because of their prosperity in Christ. Their riches led some to pride, costly apparel, fine pearls, division into classes, and the building of churches for gain.

l: the division among the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: In the two hundred and thirty and first year, there was a great division among the people. The true believers were called Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites, while those who rejected the gospel were called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites.

l: the records hidden by Ammaron, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ, opening
s: The records hidden by Ammaron were sacred records handed down from generation to generation. Ammaron hid them unto the Lord so they might come again unto the remnant of the house of Jacob according to the Lord’s prophecies and promises.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Mormon records what he has seen and heard in the Book of Mormon record. Ammaron instructs Mormon to remember what he observes, retrieve the plates of Nephi at the hill Shim when he is twenty-four, and engrave his observations on them. The Nephites and Lamanites fight near Zarahemla, followed by about four years of peace, but wickedness and unbelief spread throughout the land. Mormon is visited by the Lord at age fifteen and tastes the goodness of Jesus, but he is forbidden to preach to the people.

l: The Book of Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Mormon calls his record of the things he has seen and heard the Book of Mormon.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Mormon is a descendant of Nephi whose father is named Mormon. He records his observations, is visited by the Lord at age fifteen, and is forbidden to preach because of the people's rebellion and hard hearts.

l: Ammaron, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Ammaron hides the records unto the Lord and instructs Mormon to retrieve the plates of Nephi and record what he observes about the people when he is twenty-four.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Mormon tastes and knows of the goodness of Jesus when he is fifteen years old.

l: Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The Lord receives the records and sacred engravings. He visits Mormon, takes away his beloved disciples because of the people's iniquity, and curses the land so that hidden treasures become slippery.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The Nephites consist of the Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites. They gather more than thirty thousand men, defeat the Lamanites in several battles, and slay many of them.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites include the Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites. They fight the Nephites near Zarahemla and later withdraw their design, while Gadianton robbers are among them.

l: the Gadianton robbers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The Gadianton robbers are among the Lamanites and infest the land. Their presence contributes to the inhabitants hiding their treasures in the earth.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Zarahemla is the land to which Mormon is carried by his father when he is eleven years old. War between the Nephites and Lamanites begins in its borders by the waters of Sidon.

l: the land, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The land becomes covered with buildings and is filled with numerous people. It is cursed because of the people's hard hearts, and sorceries, witchcrafts, and magics occur throughout it.

l: records, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Ammaron hides the records unto the Lord and tells Mormon where the sacred engravings concerning the people have been deposited.

l: plates of Nephi, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Ammaron tells Mormon to take the plates of Nephi for himself and engrave on them what he has observed concerning the people.

l: the Book of Mormon record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The Book of Mormon record contains Mormon's account of the things he has seen and heard and his observations concerning the people.

l: the people, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The people become numerous, wicked, and unbelieving. Their iniquity causes miracles, healing, gifts from the Lord, and the Holy Ghost to cease, and their hard hearts prevent Mormon from preaching to them.

l: the war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: The war begins among the Nephites and Lamanites in the borders of Zarahemla by the waters of Sidon. The Nephites win several battles, and the Lamanites withdraw their design.

l: peace, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Peace is settled in the land after the Lamanites withdraw their design. It remains for about four years without bloodshed.

l: wickedness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record / Chapter 1
s: Wickedness prevails across the whole land and causes the Lord to take away his beloved disciples. It is accompanied by unbelief, sorceries, witchcrafts, and magics.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Mormon leads the Nephites in renewed wars against the Lamanites as the Nephites are repeatedly driven from their lands and cities. The land is filled with robbers, Lamanites, blood, carnage, wickedness, and abominations, while the Nephites’ sorrow does not result in true repentance. Mormon records the people’s wickedness on the plates of Nephi and mourns their spiritual decline. After further battles, the Nephites and their enemies make a treaty dividing the lands of inheritance between them.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Mormon is appointed leader of the Nephite armies while still young because he is large in stature. He leads battles, urges the Nephites to defend their families and homes, records their wickedness on the plates of Nephi, and sorrows over their destruction and abominations.

l: Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The Lord’s mercies and long-suffering cause Mormon to hope that the Nephites will become righteous again. The strength of the Lord is not with the Nephites because of their wickedness, and the Spirit of the Lord does not abide in them.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites fight the Lamanites but are repeatedly frightened, driven from cities and lands, and hunted northward. They briefly defeat larger Lamanite armies, yet remain weakened by wickedness and later divide their inherited lands with the Lamanites and robbers of Gadianton.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The Lamanites attack the Nephites with great power, drive them from Angola, the land of David, and other places, and pursue them northward. They are led by Aaron in one battle and later make a treaty that gives them the land southward.

l: the Gadianton robbers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The robbers of Gadianton contribute to the wickedness and destruction in the land. They fight against the Nephites and later participate with the Lamanites in a treaty dividing the lands of inheritance.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The Nephite armies retreat when frightened by the Lamanites, defend fortified cities, and fight several battles under Mormon’s leadership. They defeat larger forces at times but are ultimately left without the strength of the Lord.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The Lamanite armies attack with exceedingly great power and drive the Nephites from their cities and lands. They are defeated in battles by Mormon’s forces but continue pursuing the Nephites before entering a treaty.

l: Shem, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Shem is a land where the Nephites are driven after fleeing northward. Mormon fortifies its city and gathers the Nephites there in an effort to save them from destruction.

l: plates of Nephi, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Mormon takes the plates of Nephi according to Ammaron’s word and makes a record on them. He records a full account of the wickedness and abominations of the people.

l: the war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: War begins again between the Nephites and the Lamanites in the same year. The conflict continues through repeated attacks, retreats, battles, widespread destruction, and eventual division of the lands by treaty.

l: treaty between the Nephites, Lamanites, and robbers of Gadianton, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: In the three hundred and fiftieth year, the Nephites make a treaty with the Lamanites and the robbers of Gadianton. The treaty divides the lands of inheritance, giving the Nephites the land northward to the narrow passage and the Lamanites the land southward.

l: destruction, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Destruction hangs over the people because of their wickedness, robbers, murders, magic art, and witchcraft. Mormon sees thousands of Nephites hewn down in rebellion and heaped upon the land.

l: blood and carnage, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Blood and carnage spread throughout the land among both the Nephites and the Lamanites. The violence becomes a complete revolution throughout the face of the land.

l: mourning and lamentation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: Mourning and lamentation begin throughout the land, especially among the Nephites, because no one can keep what is his own. Mormon initially rejoices at their sorrow but later recognizes that it is not true repentance.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites begin to repent of their iniquity and cry as Samuel the prophet had prophesied. Their sorrow is not unto repentance through the goodness of God, and they do not come to Jesus with broken hearts and contrite spirits.

l: wickedness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 2
s: The people’s wickedness and abominations fill the land and persist throughout Mormon’s life. Mormon records a full account of them on the plates of Nephi and says that their wickedness causes him continual sorrow.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites resumed battle against the Nephites after ten years, but the Nephites defeated them in two successive years. The Lord called the Nephites to repent, be baptized, and rebuild his church, but they hardened their hearts. Mormon refused to continue leading them because of their wickedness, after the Nephites vowed vengeance against their enemies. Mormon testified that all people will stand before the judgment-seat of Christ and urged them to believe the gospel of Jesus Christ and repent.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites prepared to battle the Nephites, came down to the city of Desolation in the three hundred and sixty-first and three hundred and sixty-second years, and were defeated. Many were slain, and their dead were cast into the sea.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites prepared their lands and arms, gathered at the land Desolation, and fortified against the Lamanites. They defeated the Lamanites twice, then boasted in their strength and swore to avenge their slain brethren.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Mormon led the Nephites many times despite their wickedness and prayed for them, but he refused to continue as their commander because of their wickedness and abomination. He stood as an idle witness and wrote to the Gentiles, the house of Israel, and all the ends of the earth.

l: Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Lord called the Nephites to repent, come unto him, be baptized, and build up his church so they could be spared. He declared that vengeance was his and that the unrepentant people would be cut off from the face of the earth.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Lord and Savior, and as the one whose gospel people should believe. He chose twelve disciples in the land of Jerusalem and will judge the house of Israel according to their works.

l: God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: God is the Nephites' Lord and is the one who spared them and granted them a chance for repentance. Mormon prayed to God for the Nephites all day long.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The house of Israel is addressed as a people who will be judged according to their works by the twelve whom Jesus chose in the land of Jerusalem. It is also told that it will be about to prepare to return to the land of its inheritance.

l: land Desolation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Mormon caused the Nephites to gather at the land Desolation to defend against the Lamanites.

l: city of Desolation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The city of Desolation was in the borders by the narrow pass leading into the land southward. The Nephites placed their armies there, and the Lamanites came down there to battle.

l: earth, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Mormon wrote to all the ends of the earth and testified that the unrepentant Nephites would be cut off from the face of the earth.

l: armies, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Nephite armies were placed at the city of Desolation and fortified against the Lamanites with all their force. The Lamanite armies came to battle and were defeated.

l: the war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites resumed battle after ten years, and the Nephites defeated them in the three hundred and sixty-first and three hundred and sixty-second years. The Nephites then vowed to go to battle against their enemies and avenge their slain brethren.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Lord called the Nephites to repentance, but they did not repent and hardened their hearts. Because they did not repent after being delivered, the Lord declared that they would be cut off from the face of the earth.

l: Nephite victories, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites defeated the Lamanites in two successive years, including a battle in which many Lamanites were slain. These victories caused the Nephites to boast in their own strength.

l: Nephite vengeance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites swore before the heavens and by the throne of God that they would avenge the blood of their brethren and cut their enemies off from the land. The Lord declared that vengeance was his.

l: wickedness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites' wickedness and abomination caused Mormon to refuse further command. Their hardness of heart and failure to repent led to the Lord's declaration that they would be cut off.

l: judgment, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Every soul belonging to the whole human family of Adam must stand before the judgment-seat of Christ and be judged according to works, whether good or evil. The house of Israel and the remnant of the Nephites will be judged by the twelve chosen by Jesus in the respective lands.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Mormon urged the ends of the earth to believe the gospel of Jesus Christ, which they would have among them. He also testified that the Jews would have another witness that Jesus was the very Christ and the very God.

l: human family of Adam, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 3
s: Every soul belonging to the whole human family of Adam must stand before the judgment-seat of Christ and be judged according to its works.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites and Lamanites engage in repeated battles over the land Desolation, city Desolation, and city Teancum. The Lamanites repeatedly defeat the Nephites, take prisoners, and sacrifice Nephite women and children to idol gods, while the Nephites persist in wickedness and sometimes boast of their strength. Mormon observes the destruction and retrieves the records that Ammaron had hidden at hill Shim. The unit describes unprecedented wickedness, bloodshed, and hardened hearts among the people.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites fight repeated battles against the Lamanites but are repeatedly driven back, slaughtered, and swept off. They persist in wickedness, boast of their strength after victories, and their women and children are taken prisoner and sacrificed.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Lamanites repeatedly attack the Nephites, take possession of city Desolation, drive inhabitants from city Teancum, and capture prisoners. They sacrifice Nephite women and children to idol gods and eventually gain continuing power over the Nephites.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: Mormon sees that the Lamanites are about to overthrow the land. He goes to hill Shim and takes up the records that Ammaron had hidden unto the Lord.

l: land Desolation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites go up with their armies from the land Desolation, are driven back there, and later flee from it after Lamanite attacks. The land is eventually about to be overthrown by the Lamanites.

l: city of Desolation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Lamanites take possession of city Desolation, the Nephites later retake it, and the Lamanites subsequently take it again. Battles in and around the city result in many deaths and the Nephites' defeat.

l: city Teancum, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: City Teancum lies near the seashore and near city Desolation. The Lamanites prepare to attack it, are initially repulsed, and later drive out its inhabitants and take many prisoners.

l: hill Shim, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: Mormon goes to hill Shim when the Lamanites are about to overthrow the land. He takes up the records that Ammaron had hidden there unto the Lord.

l: records, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The records had been hidden by Ammaron unto the Lord. Mormon takes them up at hill Shim when the Lamanites are about to overthrow the land.

l: the war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The battles continue for many years and cause thousands to be slain on both sides. The Lamanites increasingly defeat and drive back the Nephites, who gain no further power over them after the three hundred and seventy and fifth year.

l: sacrifices of women and children, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Lamanites take Nephite women and children prisoner and offer them as sacrifices to idol gods. This causes the Nephites great anger and leads them to defeat and drive the Lamanites out of their lands temporarily.

l: wickedness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites do not repent of the evil they have done and persist in wickedness. The unit states that such great wickedness had never before existed among the children of Lehi or the house of Israel, and that the wicked stir up bloodshed.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: Mormon returns to assist the Nephites and commands their armies, but the Lamanites eventually overwhelm and destroy the Nephites despite their resistance. Mormon writes an abridgment of the bloodshed and explains that hidden things will be revealed to the remnant of the people and to the Gentiles. The record concerns the scattering and future restoration of the house of Israel, the belief of the Jews and their seed in Jesus, and warnings to the Gentiles to repent. The chapter teaches that unbelief, idolatry, and wickedness bring destruction, while God remembers covenants and the prayers of the righteous.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: Mormon repents of his oath not to assist the Nephites and again commands their armies. He witnesses their destruction, writes a small abridgment because of a commandment, and warns the Gentiles to repent.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Nephites give Mormon command of their armies and maintain several cities against the Lamanites. In the three hundred and eightieth year they are overwhelmed, and those who cannot escape are destroyed.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Lamanites repeatedly invade Nephite lands and are driven back from some cities. They eventually overcome the Nephites and destroy the inhabitants, towns, villages, and cities left behind.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The Gentiles are said to scatter the Nephites and possess the land. They will receive the reserved blessings, care for the house of Israel, receive its gospel, and are warned to repent and humble themselves before God.

l: Jews, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record, Chapter 5
s: The record will go to the unbelieving Jews so they may be persuaded that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Through Jesus, the Father will restore the Jews, or all the house of Israel, to the land of their inheritance.
